'''Tita Kovač Artemis''' (19 September 1930 – 11 March 2016) was a [[Slovenes|Slovene]] [[chemist]] and writer.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.dolenjskilist.si/2016/03/14/151586/novice/dolenjska/Umrla_pisateljica_in_castna_obcanka_Novega_mesta_Tita_Kovac_Artemis/|title=Umrla pisateljica in častna občanka Novega mesta Tita Kovač Artemis|work=Dolenjski list|accessdate=19 March 2016}}</ref>

She won the [[Levstik Award]] in 1985 for her book ''Kemiki skozi stoletja'' (Chemists Through the Centuries).<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.mladinska.com/knjige/knjizne_nagrade/levstikove__nagrade|title=Levstikove nagrade|work=Mladinska knjiga|accessdate=19 March 2016}}</ref>

She was best known for her documented [[biographical novel]]s on [[Johann Weikhard von Valvasor]] ''Spomini baraona Valvasorja'' (''Memoirs of Baron Valvasor''), 1973; [[Stephen Uroš III Dečanski of Serbia|Stephen Dečanski]] ''Štefan Dečanski'', 1974; [[Sigmund Zois]] ''Najbogatejši Kranjec'' (''The Richest Carniolan''), 1979; [[Janez Bleiweis]] ''Slovenski orator'' (The Slovene Orator), 1990; and [[Ioannis Kapodistrias]] ''Grški feniks'' (''The Greek Phoenix''), 2003.{{citation needed|date=March 2016}}

In 1970 she moved to [[Greece]] where she lived and worked for many years until she moved to a retirement home near [[Topolšica]] in her native Slovenia.<ref>[http://www.cs-zimzelen.si/176 PV Zimzelen site] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120508070602/http://www.cs-zimzelen.si/176 |date=8 May 2012 }}, cs-zimzelen.si; accessed 20 March 2016.</ref>
